solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Superior aristocrat occupying singular times

blocks.note: a nob is a toff, an aristocrat
times = by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A superior aristocrat lording it over a single era of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like a stretch of history; here it is the multiplication sign, read as 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snobby acts superior, looking down on others.

clue.text: Smart dons modelled certain type of weather

indicators.note: clay that is modelled is reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Well-dressed university lecturers posing as models for a weather feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modelled' reads as a catwalk verb for the smart dons; it only asks for the letters to be reshaped.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandstorm is a particular kind of weather, wind laden with sand.

clue.text: Magical schoolboy without power to be animal

blocks.note: p = power, the physics symbol; removed

explanation.surface: A boy wizard, stripped of his power, turned into an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a transfiguration spell; the real magic is dropping one letter from the wizard's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is an animal, a river-dwelling mammal.

clue.text: SF author beginning to recover, restricted by inferior implant

blocks.note: bad = inferior, poor quality; it holds the R
to implant is to bury, set deep in

explanation.surface: A science-fiction writer on the mend after a botched implant.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray Bradbury wrote Fahrenheit 451. 'Implant' feels like surgery in the surface; it is simply 'bury'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray Bradbury was an American science-fiction (SF) author.

clue.text: Examination in science ultimately failing a student

blocks.note: L = learner, the L-plate on a student driver's car

explanation.surface: A student fails the science exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a failed science paper; the 'examination' is in fact a medical check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical sense, chiefly American: the adjective used as a noun names the doctor's routine check-up of the body.

clue.text: Secret term used in golf, also one in soccer?

explanation.surface: Asking for a secret piece of jargon shared by golf and football.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a sporting-glossary question; it is three words laid end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hole-and-corner means secret or furtive, done out of sight.

clue.text: Stumped about pine shampoo container?

blocks.note: st = stumped in cricket scoring; it wraps round ACHE
to pine is to ache, to yearn

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a pine-scented shampoo bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the scent of the shampoo; it is the verb, to long for. ST is the scorecard abbreviation for stumped, a way a batsman is out in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed packet, often of shampoo; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Sausage and fruit with soft drink around? Cheers

blocks.note: cola, a fizzy soft drink; it goes round HIP
a rose hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A pub order: a sausage, some fruit and a soft drink, with a thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like a toast; in British speech it also means thanks, which is TA. A chipolata is a small thin sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: this small, thin pork link, a British breakfast and Christmas-dinner staple, is one kind of sausage.

clue.text: Late arrival missing a good beer

blocks.note: a lagger lags behind, arriving late

explanation.surface: Someone turns up late and misses out on a good beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a latecomer losing his pint; the missing thing is only a G.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a light, cold-fermented brew is one kind of beer, the commonest in British pubs.

clue.text: King’s mistress about to be announced in court affair?

blocks.note: Nell Gwyn, mistress of Charles II; she wraps round TBA
TBA = to be announced, as on a programme

explanation.surface: A royal mistress whose role in a scandal at court is yet to be revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court affair' paints a royal scandal; the court is a sports court. Nell Gwyn was Charles II's best-known mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a game played on a court; the question mark flags the pun on 'court affair'.

clue.text: Book not so much about revolutionary rebel’s aim

indicators.note: the letters are turned over, overthrown, into a new order

blocks.note: less = not so much; it wraps round the anagram

explanation.surface: A book questioning how much the revolutionary rebel really wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting, since Victor Hugo's novel is full of revolutionary rebels at the barricades.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Misérables is Victor Hugo's novel, a book.

clue.text: Idle though not at first inadequate

explanation.surface: An idler who, though not at first, turns out to be inadequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' is an adjective in the surface but needs to be read as the participle 'slacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking means inadequate, falling short.

clue.text: Daphne, perhaps, in personnel aboard vessel

blocks.note: HR = human resources, the personnel department

explanation.surface: A woman called Daphne serving among the crew on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Daphne looks like a person's name; it is a genus of flowering shrubs, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps': Daphne is a genus of scented flowering bushes, one instance of the class.

clue.text: Recalled origins when going around old part of theatre

indicators.note: called back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: roots = origins; turned round to STOOR and split around AGED

explanation.surface: Remembering one's early days in an old theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reads as memory; it means called back, so the word runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage door is the part of a theatre where performers come and go.

clue.text: 50 per cent of Noel Coward is reconstituted from this writer

indicators.note: put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One witty playwright partly rebuilt from another.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward and Oscar Wilde were both celebrated wits and playwrights, which is what makes the surface ring true.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the Irish writer of The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: Cape state — definitely not American — offering lots of room

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A spacious home in a Cape province that insists it is not American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a place beside 'Cape' and 'American'; it is the verb, to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cavernous is vast inside, offering lots of room.

clue.text: Secure network finally penetrated

explanation.surface: A supposedly secure computer network that has finally been hacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure' reads as an adjective about the network; it is the verb, as in land a fish or a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: To land something is to secure it, as in landing a deal.

clue.text: Distribution is adopted by pedlars on the move

blocks.note: anagram of PEDLARS, split around IS

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen taking on the job of distributing goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about sales rounds; the travelling pedlars are only letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: spreading things out over an area is distributing them.

clue.text: I’m working with US soldier, reversing US city disgrace

indicators.note: the letters so far are put into reverse

explanation.surface: An American soldier in disgrace after backing out of a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers everything before it, IMONGI turning into IGNOMI, and New York is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both nouns name public shame and loss of standing.

clue.text: Almost finished after master’s opening gambit

blocks.note: OVER = finished, less its last letter

explanation.surface: A chess master's opening gambit, and the game is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening gambit' reads as a single chess phrase; it has to be split, 'opening' going with 'master's' and 'gambit' standing alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is a calculated move, in chess or otherwise.

clue.text: Source of oil, something disappointing provided by shop

blocks.note: a lemon is a dud, something that disappoints
to shop and to grass both mean to inform on someone

explanation.surface: An oil product that turns out disappointing when bought from a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' looks like a store; it is the British slang verb for informing on someone to the police, as is 'grass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by function: this tropical plant is distilled for a citrus-scented essential oil used in soaps and cooking.

clue.text: Tense, ahead of number showing restraint

blocks.note: a number is something that numbs, as ether does

explanation.surface: Someone tense ahead of a number, holding themselves back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure: read it as numb-er, a thing that numbs, which is the anaesthetic ether.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or chain that restrains an animal.

clue.text: Carbon in rocks cracking ordinary eggshell?

blocks.note: plain = ordinary; it is split open by ORCE
ore is metal-bearing rock; it holds the C

explanation.surface: A carbon-rich stone cracking an ordinary egg's shell.
explanation.walkthrough: Eggshell is a thin, fine kind of porcelain; the question mark flags that the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell porcelain is a very thin, translucent china, so eggshell is a kind of porcelain.

clue.text: Pressure on guide to provide appeal

explanation.surface: Leaning on a guide to make an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places P ahead of LEAD; the surface pressure is a physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: to beg earnestly for something is to appeal.

clue.text: Veteran fighter removing outer clothing

blocks.note: a soldier is a fighter; S and R, the outer letters, go

explanation.surface: An old soldier stripping off his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Veteran fighter' reads as one phrase for an old soldier; it has to be split, with 'Veteran' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: an old-timer, someone long in the tooth, is a veteran in the loose sense.

clue.text: Road up? Concede flood

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading bottom to top, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: to own (up) is to admit, concede

explanation.surface: Admitting that a dug-up road has flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road up' looks like the roadworks sign; in a down clue, up means the letters read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: to submerge completely is to flood, as when a river swamps the fields.

clue.text: Historic vestment rotated by 50 per cent? Not quite

indicators.note: turned round end to end, so the word runs backwards
the word falls just short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: a cope is a priest's long cloak-like vestment

explanation.surface: An old church vestment turned halfway round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotated by 50 per cent' reads as a half turn; 'by' only joins, and the 50 per cent is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal means marking an epoch, so historic.

clue.text: Very expensive sport, I sense

explanation.surface: Someone sensing that a pastime costs far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I sense' reads as a verb phrase; 'sense' is the noun, NOUS, British slang for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ruinous costs so much it could ruin you.

clue.text: Suspicion I’d held back son in parade

indicators.note: held backwards, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: as written, then turned to DI
to strut is to parade; it holds S

explanation.surface: Someone harbouring doubts after holding their son back from a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held back' sounds like restraint; it only turns I'D round.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a want of faith in someone's honesty is suspicion of them.

clue.text: Collection of religious texts disheartened holy men a lot at first

indicators.note: each word loses its heart, its middle letters

blocks.note: HOLY without its middle letters OL

explanation.surface: Dispirited holy men going through a lot of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' sounds like the holy men's mood; it strips the middles from both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: a church's book of hymns gathers sacred songs, religious texts, in one volume.
